answer: Each identity must fund its bond from outside the system. It locks 100 credit in a willow registry and files one ember receipt proving an external deposit; one receipt funds only one identity. A crystal auditor recomputes the origin chain from public records, and an internally funded bond is rejected with its 15 credit fee burned. The k-th fake still needs a fresh 100 bond plus 15 fee, so 1,000 fakes cost 115,000 credit. An internal-recycling ring fails because the auditor traces each ember receipt to its external source. An honest agent posts once and recovers its bond on exit.
